newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-LUYENDYK EARNS SECOND INDY 500 POLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LUYENDYK EARNS SECOND INDY 500 POLE.

text.p: Dutchman Arie Luyendyk earned his second Indy 500 pole on Saturday with a four-lap average speed of 218.263 mph (351.251 kph) in a G-Force Oldsmobile.

Luyendyk, team owner Fred Treadway and team engineer Tim Wardrop decided early to gamble by taking whatever speed they got out of the first qualifying run and hope that the powerful Menard Racing Team would not go any faster.

The gamble worked, partly because his rival team had decided after 3,000 miles of testing with Firestone tires to switch to Goodyear tires, then went back to Firestones two days later, leaving Menard two days behind in testing.
"We figured out between Fred Treadway, Tim Wardrop, and myself you can run only so many laps to get it right," said Luyendyk, who won the Indy 500 in 1990 and earned a pole in 1993.

"It's too bad I couldn't get into the '19s (219 mph) on this qualifying run, but you have to say to yourself sometimes, OK, that's it, that's all I'm going to get out of this on this particular run, so I'll take it."
When Stewart went out later in the day he was only slightly slower at 218.021 mph (350.861 kph). "We just ran out of time," said Stewart.
Rookie Vincenzo Sospiri of Italy, who drove for the defunct Lola Formula One team this year, was third fastest at 216.822 mph (348.932 kph) in a Dallara Oldsmobile.
A total of 21 drivers including five rookies qualified for the 500-mile race to be run on May 25. There will be 33 in the field after qualifying Sunday and next weekend.
